newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-BRYANT TAKES TWO-SHOT LEAD AT TUCSON CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BRYANT TAKES TWO-SHOT LEAD AT TUCSON CLASSIC.

text.p: Brad Bryant charged out of the gate Saturday then held on to post a five-under-par 67 Saturday and grab a two-stroke lead after the third round of the Tucson Classic.
Bryant finished the day at 12 under par, two ahead of overnight leader Steve Jones, who shot a 72, and last week's winner, Paul Stankowski, who shot 69.

One of the keys to scoring at Tucson National is to play well on the first eight holes, which generally allow wedge or short-iron approach shots. Bryant birdied five of the eight, Jones and Stankowski each birdied just one.
"I'm a little surprised to be leading, actually," said Bryant. "I thought Steve or one of the other guys would do a little better today," said Bryant.

The last time Bryant led after three rounds was the 1995 Walt Disney World Classic, which was all that mattered that week, as the event was rain-shortened to 54 holes. It was his 475th official PGA Tour event, and his first win.

"The pressure of winning is off me a bit, now that I'm no longer the guy who's played the longest without a win. Now, I'm just trying to earn enough money to retire in two years and go fishing," said the 42-year-old Bryant.
Jones, who had started with a three-stroke lead, had been expected by many to put on a performance similar to last month's domination of the Phoenix Open, which he won by 11 shots.
"Boring and frustrating - those are two words that describe my round today," said Jones.

"God tells us to be thankful for all things, but on days like this it's tough to be thankful. I guess I'm thankful that I didn't lose the tournament today, and hopefully this will be my one bad round of the week."

Stankowski, who had four birdies and a three-putt bogey on his card, wasn't sure what his chances were to win back-to-back in Tucson on Sunday. Twice in the last 11 months he has won, and then immediately won again in his next start.

"I don't know what the odds are for me doing it a third time," he said. "But I'm playing with a lot of confidence right now, and I've certainly put myself in position to pull it off. If I succeed, the only thing I have to figure out is how to play well three weeks in a row."
